title: Record the team strategy for root coders and coding delegations
outcome: Record the team strategy for root coders and coding delegations
acceptance: A short Engram document under docs/ (cross-linked from docs/development.md or the nearest coordination doc) states the team strategy: root sessions take independent claimed packages, each with its own worktree, evidence and landing; coding delegations take bounded parallel subwork whose parent integrates, verifies and lands it; root count matches ready disjoint packages and host capacity (serial full gates, build/memory limits); the strategy is reassessed from measured throughput and failures, naming which measurements.

It links TermAl's root-session API documentation for creation and states the provenance an Engram coordinator records on the item when it creates a root (creator, project/cwd, explicit model, purpose, receipt), without restating TermAl's contract.

It grants and changes no commit, push, tracker, approval, restart or deploy authority, and changes no gate or review rule; the Engram and TermAl coordinators' concurrence on the final wording is recorded in this item's notes before landing.

completion.summary:
Delivered docs/team-strategy.md (cross-linked from docs/development.md), with the wording both coordinators concurred on: Engram::Fable #2543 and Termal::Fable2 #207.
- Roots take one independent package each and land under their project's rules (Engram's Authority and Git).
- Delegations are bounded subwork that the parent integrates, verifies and lands.
- Root count is limited by ready disjoint packages and host capacity (one full gate at a time, a filtered-test limit, the commit-charge threshold).
- Idle roots are reused first.
- Reassessment uses landings per hour, gate failures by class, peak commit charge, review rounds and idle root-hours.
- It links the creation routes on TermAl's root-session page (#choosing-a-route at 536c17a1) and lists the creation provenance a coordinator records.
- It grants and changes no authority or gate/review rule, and governs over restatements elsewhere.
